allocation_comparison: All 643 allocation/size records match the actual 0.4 baseline byte-for-byte; latency was measured separately without allocation instrumentation.
cache_context: Three initial cache-dependent oracle/MSRV/Clippy checks stalled without compiler progress and were deliberately terminated (exit 143). Wrapper-free isolated-target replacements passed; canceled checks are not passing evidence.
assessment: Eager two-hint iteration improved sparse eviction but slowed inherited reads. The retained lazy implementation preserves original-hit behavior: inherited read median changes range -1.21% to +0.30% across horizons 1/8/32/128/512. Evicted collection p50 improves 67.9–74.2% for horizons 1–128 and full correction 22.5–62.8%; horizon 512 stays near baseline. Other timeline threshold exceedances remain unresolved and are retained, not accepted.
limitations: Shared host, five alternating run-level distributions, 200 samples/profile after 16 warmups; no statistical speedup/noninferiority proof or final release performance pass.
Original slow sparse fallback existed at both baseline and prior candidate; this optimization removes work but does not by itself explain every prior baseline/candidate slowdown.
Exact-path and canonical/ancestor precedence remains native. Arbitrary imported/recycled layouts can still require a bounded full scan.
No allocation increase does not prove a stack high-water bound. Portable compilation and bounded local indices are qualified, not a new measured stack ceiling.
Final coverage, full chaos and exact final-candidate qualification remain open.
